auditor.notes: Fresh isolated subagent (round 2, after the planner's targeted revision). Inputs were the plan directory (out/ only), the plan-auditor skill, and the shared glossary. The repo fixture (candidate/work/repo), the planning conversation, and all evaluation files were not read. Every round-1 finding was re-verified against the current artifacts themselves, not against the run-manifest's claim of resolution.

findings.evidence: stage-contract.json shared_contracts C1 spec: 'consumer.job_timeout resolves job['timeout_ms'] if present, else job['timeout'] (draft key, backward-compatible fallback), else DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000)' and tasks/T01.json failure_cases[2]: 'job carries both "timeout_ms": 500 and "timeout": 123 → job_timeout returns 500 — timeout_ms wins per C1 precedence order'. No acceptance test in the plan exercises the both-keys case: tasks/T02.json implementation_constraints pins 'Exactly 5 test methods', none of which uses a dict carrying both keys (method (1) pins assertNotIn('timeout', job) on make_job output, so producer-built jobs never carry both keys), and T03's three seam tests (round-trip, missing-timeout default + draft-key fallback, engine boundary) likewise. A wrong-order implementation resolving the draft 'timeout' key before 'timeout_ms' would still pass A1-A5 (every producer-built job carries only 'timeout_ms'), so the frozen regression suite — whose stated purpose is that 'any future drift on seams S1/S2 fails the suite' (tasks/T02.json objective) — would not detect a C1 precedence inversion. The only protection is that the T01 executor actually exercises its own failure_cases checklist mid-run.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the precedence case in the frozen suite: repurpose T02 method (3) to assert the hand-crafted dict {'timeout_ms': 500, 'timeout': 123} → 500 (keeps the 'Exactly 5 test methods' count, no count churn anywhere), or add it as a fourth seam test in T03 with the pinned counts updated in one coordinated pass (T02 'Exactly 5' → 6, A4 'Ran 5 tests' → 6, A5/T04-AT4/E4 '15' → 16, E3/T04-AT3 '8' → 9). Re-run plan-check lint after either change.

findings.evidence: tasks/T01.json acceptance_tests T01-AT2.description: 'consumer.job_timeout(producer.make_job('j2', {'cmd': 'y'})) returns 30000 (default timeout_ms branch)' — but T01-AT2.evidence: 'python -m unittest tests.test_consumer -v → 'Ran 3 tests ... OK', exit code 0 (test_job_timeout_default green)'. Per input.md repo notes, tests/test_consumer.py's 3 tests pin 'the draft timeout key (job_timeout({"timeout": 123}) == 123), the {} default (30000), and validate_job'; none of them runs the make_job default-timeout_ms case, and test_job_timeout_default exercises the empty-dict DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS branch — a different branch than the one the description names. The cited command is decidable, but it verifies a different case than the one described; the named case is only covered indirectly by T01-AT1/A1 (non-default 500).
findings.suggested_fix: Align evidence with case: either reword T01-AT2.description to what test_job_timeout_default actually pins ('{} → 30000 via DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS stays green after T01'), or replace the evidence with a literal check of the named case (a one-line python -c assertion job_timeout(make_job('j2', {'cmd': 'y'})) == 30000 → exit code 0).
